title: Compound interest
subject: Math
learningGoal: Apply A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) to compute compound growth.
spokenLines: Compound interest — the money you earn also earns money.
The formula: A equals P times, one plus r over n, all raised to n t.
P is principal. r is rate. n is times per year compounded. t is years.
Say you invest one thousand dollars at five percent, compounded yearly, for ten years.
P is one thousand. r is zero point zero five. n is one. t is ten.
So A equals one thousand times one point zero five to the tenth.
One point zero five to the tenth is about one point six two nine.
A is about one thousand six hundred twenty nine dollars.
So five percent for ten years grows a thousand into sixteen twenty nine.

actions.text: P principal, r rate, n periods/yr, t years
